competences: The learner identifies the term's source-grounded facts about end of term assessment.
The learner answers questions about Uganda as an independent nation, The Government of Uganda, Population, Size and Distribution correctly.
languageCompetence: Reads and spells words associated with independence, government, population, election, census.
objectives: By the end of the period, learners should be able to identify the sourced facts about end of term assessment.
By the end of the period, learners should be able to answer the available original questions on Uganda as an independent nation, The Government of Uganda, Population, Size and Distribution.
priorKnowledge: Learners have studied SST topics about independent Uganda, the government and population during this term. They use their earlier notes while reviewing end of term assessment.
materials: SST revision chart on end of term assessment
P5 SST reference notes and original exercise questions
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher introduces end of term assessment and reviews relevant earlier Primary Five work. They ask "Give two differences in the activities run by the central and local government." and connect the replies with the original source material.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall prior SST knowledge, answer the opening question and identify the earlier topics that relate to the new work.

steps.content: The end of term assessment covers 20 questions on the studied topics.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher distributes the sourced assessment questions, tells pupils how to number their responses and explains the examination rules. They confirm that all pupils can read the questions without supplying answers.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the instructions, prepare to answer independently and arrange their answer books with the correct question numbers.

steps.content: Give two differences in the activities run by the central and local government. | What is the ruling body of government called? | Who is the local of all ministers in government? | What role do civil servants play in government? | Which organ of the government is known as the custodian of the law? | Write down four ways to show how people benefit from the government. | What title was given to the leader of government in1961 ? | Which title was given to the leader of government in1962 – 1966? | Which constitution granted Uganda independence ? | What is a government? | State any three roles performed by the government. | State any three problems the government faces when performing iots duties.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher supervises individual responses and monitors time. They ensure all pupils can attempt the original questions, including "Give two differences in the activities run by the central and local government." and "What is the ruling body of government called?", without giving answers or adding invented tasks.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners attempt the original written questions individually, use earlier class knowledge and review their work before submitting.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher collects completed work and checks that the pupils have numbered their answers correctly. They explain that the completed assessment will be marked using the original source material.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners submit their written answers, make sure their books are named and leave their places ready for the next class activity.

assessment: Use the original questions "Give two differences in the activities run by the central and local government." and "What is the ruling body of government called?", with the remaining sourced exercise, to check individual learners' understanding. Mark against the source facts.
homework: Revise and complete the remaining original questions including "State any three problems the government faces when conducting a national population"
